item.title: How this New York City community cleanup project is helping adults make new friends
item.description: Making new friends as an adult can be challenging, but some people are finding new connections through charity work. Michael George shows us how volunteering is bringing people together.

item.title: U.K.-Iranian national released on bail after arrest in security incident near base
item.description: The 25-year-old man was arrested in London, and police searched two properties in the U.K. capital, Counter Terrorism Policing said.

item.title: U.K. police accuse 2 Iranian men of planning terror attack on Jewish community
item.description: Two Iranian men have been charged with plotting a terror attack on the Jewish community in Manchester, British police said.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 4)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Inside the London social club for VIP puppies
item.description: The social scene isn't just for people anymore. Pet owners are making sure their four-legged friends get in on it. CBS's Tina Kraus takes us to a hot new hangout for pups.

item.title: Senior Trump administration officials met to discuss Iran war at Camp David
item.description: Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth were among the officials to meet on Friday to discuss a path forward.

item.title: 11-year-old cancer survivor shares his story
item.description: About 500,000 cancer survivors were first diagnosed under the age of 20 in the U.S, according to the National Cancer Institute. Michael George has one boy's story.

item.title: Medical plane missing near Nantucket with 6 on board, authorities say
item.description: The jet was flying from Bermuda to Boston when it lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration early on Saturday.

item.title: Trump urges daylight saving time bill supporters to personally call Sen. Cotton
item.description: President Trump urged supporters to call what appears to be the senator's personal cellphone number.

item.title: Zach Bryan wears "Free Palestine" shirt during concert at Gillette Stadium
item.description: After Macklemore was barred from opening for Ed Sheeran at Gillette Stadium for pro-Palestinian comments, musician Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" shirt during his Friday show.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: The War and Treaty performs "It'll Hurt Me More Than It'll Hurt You"
item.description: Dynamic duo Tanya Trotter and Michael Trotter Jr. are behind The War and Treaty, a Grammy-nominated band known for their high-energy, crowd-pleasing performances. The married duo just release an expanded edition of their album "The Story of Michael and Tanya." Here's The War and Treaty with "It'll Hurt Me More Than It'll Hurt You."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: The War and Treaty performs "Keep You Warm Tonight"
item.description: Dynamic duo Tanya Trotter and Michael Trotter Jr. are behind The War and Treaty, a Grammy-nominated band known for their high-energy, crowd-pleasing performances. The married duo just release an expanded edition of their album "The Story of Michael and Tanya." Here's The War and Treaty with "Keep You Warm Tonight."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: The War and Treaty performs "Shouldn't Have"
item.description: Dynamic duo Tanya Trotter and Michael Trotter Jr. are behind The War and Treaty, a Grammy-nominated band known for their high-energy, crowd-pleasing performances. The married duo just release an expanded edition of their album "The Story of Michael and Tanya." Here's The War and Treaty with "Shouldn't Have."

item.title: This young designer wants to make golf comfortable and stylish
item.description: Teen designer Kate Korngold realized she could turn her sketches into functional fashion. She joins "CBS Saturday Morning" to share how she built Featherie, a women's golf apparel brand.

item.title: Tennessee prison system head to resign after failed Christa Pike execution
item.description: Christa Pike remains alive but unconscious and intubated after her failed execution on Wednesday, her lawyers said.

item.title: French police clash with student protesters over school improvement demonstrations
item.description: Student demonstrators in France are demanding improvements for the country's education systems. As protests have grown, there have been some violent clashes with police. Holly Williams has more details.

item.title: Why Trump is campaigning in red states ahead of the general election
item.description: Many Americans say they're frustrated with the economy in recent polling. President Trump is campaigning in reliably red states as November elections draw near. Aaron Navarro has what you need to know.

item.title: Chef Farideh Sadeghin shares "The Hot Dog Cookbook"
item.description: Some may think there's only one way to prepare a proper hot dog. Chef Farideh Sadeghin is here to prove that wrong with her cooking guide, "The Hot Dog Cookbook."

item.title: Alice Cooper on the evolution of his alter ego
item.description: Alice Cooper brings Anthony Mason backstage to one of his shows to talk about how he created his unforgettable alter ego ahead of the release of his new memoir, "Devil on My Shoulder."

item.title: Wang Cong to face Natalia Silva in fight for UFC 332 women's featherweight title
item.description: The Ultimate Fighting Championship women's featherweight championship is on the line as Natalia Silva and Wang Cong meet in the UFC 332 main event. For the first time ever, the full main card will be simulcast on CBS and on Paramount+. UFC analyst Paul Felder breaks it down.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Inside ICE's deportation surge
item.description: Camilo Montoya-Galvez observed Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents as they went to arrest a man. This comes as ICE has come under renewed scrutiny, a month away from November's midterm elections.

item.title: Hiring slows, unemployment ticks up in latest jobs report
item.description: The latest jobs report showed faltering numbers, and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. Jill Schlesinger weighs in.

item.title: Hawaii sea arch collapses into Pacific Ocean after storms batter island state
item.description: The Holei Sea Arch, located in the Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, was about 90 feet high before it collapsed.

item.title: More details emerge about FlyDubai co-pilot who tried to crash plane
item.description: Questions about the motive of the co-pilot who tried to crash a packed flight from Dubai to Israel continue to swirl.

item.title: 10/3: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: A look inside ICE operations, plus a young fashion designer wants to make golf more stylish and comfortable. All this and more.

item.title: Iowa approves pricy foreign-owned steel plant project in swing district
item.description: President Trump said Monday that the largest steel plant in U.S. history will be built in Iowa. It touched off a week of debate.

item.title: Professor to present findings questioning whether Epstein killed himself
item.description: Michael Freeman plans to publish his research and the New York City Medical Examiner's Epstein autopsy files.

item.title: American Airlines will let travelers mix cash and miles to pay for flights
item.description: As holiday airfares spike, American Airlines plans to let travelers pay for flights with a mix of cash and loyalty points.

item.title: Amazon vows to invest $1 billion in areas where it builds data centers
item.description: Amazon said it will invest $1 billion over five years to support job education, energy affordability and other priorities in communities where its data centers are located.
